title: One of America's Most Haunted Roads Is Not Far From Rockford
excerpt: Bray Road in Elkhorn, Wisconsin, ranks fifth among America's most haunted roads, thanks in part to the legendary Beast of Bray Road.
content:
Most people don't think twice about driving down a country road in Wisconsin. But one road near Rockford might make you reconsider, especially after dark.

While most of us worry about a deer jumping in front of our car this time of year, apparently we should be watching for werewolves, too.

READ MORE: Do You Know About The Wisconsin Werewolf?

Wisconsin's Bray Road Ranks Among America's Most Haunted Roads

Rental car company SIXT studied America's most haunted roads using TikTok and Google search trends and found a road in Wisconsin ranked in the top five, beating out some truly famous spooky locations.

Bray Road in Elkhorn ranked fifth because it has a bad reputation, apparently because a beast likes to hang out there. Dubbed the Beast of Bray Road, people claim to have seen a mysterious, wolf-like creature that is part of Wisconsin folklore.

The Legend of Wisconsin's Beast of Bray Road

That's just enough "nope' that if I'm ever on Bray Road, I'm looking for another way home.

The Beast of Bray Road has become so popular that it's inspired books, documentaries, and even a horror movie.

Rockford's Own Haunted Roads Have Some Creepy Legends

Closer to home, I'd nominate Kennedy Hill, thanks to the Bride of Kennedy Hill legend, and you can't mention creepy roads without mentioning Bloods Point Road. I mean, the name itself should make it an automatic qualifier among haunted roads.

Have you ever seen anything weird or strange on Bray Road, Kennedy Hill, Bloods Point, or anywhere else around Rockford? I'd love to hear about. Well, kind of; I just want to know which roads to avoid late at night.
